data.body:
Goal:
Introduce the membership layer: every leader knows the other leaders
via a small declarative file, and a new leader can bootstrap by
rsync'ing from an existing one. No daemon, no service discovery — the
membership is a config file you edit; bootstrap is a one-shot copy.

Verification:
1. New file `secrets/thimble.peers.toml` (TOML) lists peers as
   [[peers]] entries with `name = "alice-laptop"` and
   `target = "alice@laptop.local:/srv/thimble/secrets"` (ssh + path).
   Plaintext is fine — peer addresses aren't secret.
2. New subcommand `thimble peer add <name> <ssh-target>` appends to peers.toml; `thimble peer remove <name>` deletes; `thimble peer list` prints.
3. New subcommand `thimble peer join <existing-peer-target>` is the bootstrap:
   - rsyncs the entire `secrets/` tree from the named peer into the local store.
   - Refuses if local store is already populated (forces operator to use --replace).
   - On success, prints "joined as peer of <existing>".
4. README "Storing and Syncing" section gains a "Onboarding a new leader" walk-through: install Thimble; configure ssh access; run `thimble peer join`; you're a leader.
5. Tests for: peers.toml round-trip; add/remove/list; bootstrap into an empty store; --replace on a populated store; refusal without --replace.
6. SECURITY.md notes that peer membership changes (adding to peers.toml) are NOT quorum-gated — adding a peer just gives them rsync rights; granting them decrypt rights still requires the recipient gate, which is unchanged.

Constraints:
- Knot ref: K-55; depends on K-53, K-54.
- Files: internal/peer/peer.go (new), internal/peer/peers_toml.go (new), internal/cli/run_peer.go (new), internal/cli/cli.go (printUsage update), README.md, SECURITY.md.
- Use the existing hand-rolled TOML helpers from internal/quorum/policy.go where applicable to avoid pulling in a TOML dep.
- Bootstrap (`peer join`) must use rsync (or scp + tar) over ssh; do NOT add a third-party Go ssh library — exec rsync.
- The peers.toml file is local-only — it is NOT distributed via the bundle. Each operator manages their own peers list. (Optional future: a "shared" peers list under quorum gating.)
- Notes: peer add does NOT itself replicate. Replicating happens on the next mutation per K-56. peer join is the one-shot pull at bootstrap.
data.title: thimble peer add/list/remove and join (bootstrap)
